title: API 570 Training in Seattle: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 570 exam prep for Puget Sound piping inspectors: CUI, injection points, dock lines and Ecology's transfer pipeline rule, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 570 Training in Seattle: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Refinery Units, Marine Terminals and Transfer Lines Around Puget Sound
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors on Puget Sound

Much of the pipe an API 570 inspector looks after in Washington runs within sight of salt water: unit piping at the refineries in Whatcom and Skagit counties and on the Tacoma tideflats, rundown lines to tankage, dock lines out to the berths and transfer lines at the marine terminals of Seattle and Tacoma. This page is for inspectors in that system, for NDT technicians and pipefitters moving toward inspection, and for engineers who sign off piping circuits.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Seattle. The API 570 course is self-paced and online, with an instructor answering questions as you work through API 570, ASME B31.3 and the recommended practices behind them. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the API 570 examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certification; the course is exam preparation, and Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Where the region's process piping runs

EIA's refinery capacity survey for the start of 2026 lists five Washington refineries, all on the water, and their hydrotreating capacity shows how much hydrogen-service piping they hold. In EIA's desulfurization category, which includes catalytic hydrotreating, the state total is 205,144 barrels per stream day of naphtha and reformer feed, 109,695 of gasoline, 45,000 of kerosene and jet fuel and 176,767 of diesel. A hydrotreater typically has a feed and effluent train, wash-water connections and amine-treating lines, which an API 570 programme splits into circuits. EIA also lists alkylate production at the HF Sinclair, Marathon and Phillips 66 plants, and acid service brings its own piping rules.

The piping continues beyond the units. Marathon says its Anacortes refinery ships products from its marine terminal by ship and barge; Ecology describes the Par Pacific site in Tacoma as an oil refinery, tank farm and marine terminal; and bp describes Cherry Point as a leading supplier of jet fuel to the Seattle and Portland international airports. In Seattle, an Ecology cleanup record describes a petroleum bulk storage and distribution terminal on Harbor Island as operating since 1948 under three owners, and in Tacoma the SeaPort Sound Terminal handles asphalt, distillate, diesel, biodiesel, ethanol and industrial oil.

Ecology's transfer pipeline rule names API 570

The Washington Department of Ecology regulates oil-handling facilities under chapter 173-180 WAC. A Class 1 facility, in the rule's definition, is any structure, equipment or pipeline other than a vessel, located on or near the state's navigable waters, that transfers oil in bulk to or from a tank vessel or pipeline. A transfer pipeline is the buried or aboveground line carrying oil to or from a tank vessel or transmission pipeline, as far as the first valve inside secondary containment, provided a discharge on the facility side of that valve would not directly reach state waters; process piping is excluded. WAC 173-180-340 then sets the rules for those lines:

  • Inspection to API 570. Transfer pipelines must be inspected in accordance with API 570, cited as the 2016 edition with Addenda 1 and 2 and the 2018 errata, or to another standard Ecology approves. As an alternative, a facility may meet the rule's coating requirements for buried lines built after May 1994.
  • Bare buried pipe. Thickness and corrosion rate must be determined at no more than half the remaining life of the pipeline or every five years, whichever is more frequent.
  • Exposed pipe. Whenever buried pipe is uncovered, the operator must examine it for external corrosion by NDE, and must find the extent of any active corrosion and repair it where necessary.
  • Cathodic protection. Systems are tested for adequacy every year, impressed-current rectifiers are inspected every two months, and stray currents are tested for and mitigated.
  • Valves and pumps. Transfer pipeline pumps and valves, and storage tank valves, are inspected annually.
  • Seismic protection. Lines need one or more measures such as flexible devices at tank connections or between pipes, supports designed against seismic motion, or automatic isolation valves that close in an earthquake.

Two lessons follow for a candidate. Ecology's rule fixes an edition, while the examination is set on the edition named on the effectivity sheet for your window, so know which one your site procedure follows. And the half-remaining-life rule for buried bare pipe is the same reasoning API 570 uses for thickness intervals, with a five-year ceiling added by the state.

Where API 570 stops on the Olympic system

Olympic Pipe Line Company's system, operated by bp as a common carrier, carries refined products from the north Sound refineries to the Puget Sound region, southwest Washington and Portland. A 2022 report by the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission's pipeline safety staff names its stations: pump stations at Cherry Point, Ferndale, Anacortes, Allen and Woodinville, the Bayview products terminal, Burlington where the lines combine, and further pump stations at Renton, Tacoma, Olympia and Castle Rock.

Mainline pipe and its stations fall under 49 CFR Part 195, and the commission's pipeline safety staff inspect them; API 570 is not the governing code there. The boundary matters because refinery and terminal piping on either side of a station valve or meter skid may belong to a different programme, and Ecology adds that transfer lines built, replaced or relocated since May 1994 across ground the facility does not control must be installed to listed Part 195 provisions where feasible. For the exam, treat Part 195 as context, because the questions are built on API 570 and B31.3.

Corrosion under insulation on a damp coastline

Puget Sound rarely freezes hard, but it is damp for much of the year, and wet insulation gets little chance to dry between storms. That makes corrosion under insulation the piping mechanism most Washington inspectors spend their time on. API 570 asks the inspection plan to address CUI on susceptible systems and gives the temperature ranges and recommended inspection extents; learn those from the edition on your effectivity sheet, because they are exactly the kind of detail that changes. Locally, look first at:

  • steam-traced and insulated heavy oil and asphalt lines, which EIA's asphalt and road oil figure for the Tacoma refinery and the SeaPort terminal's product list both imply;
  • damaged jacketing at supports, penetrations, insulation rings and low points where water collects;
  • lines in intermittent or cycling service that pass in and out of the susceptible range;
  • dock lines and trestle piping exposed to spray;
  • insulated austenitic stainless lines, where wet insulation carrying chlorides can drive external stress corrosion cracking.

Expect exam questions on where CUI concentrates, which inspection techniques find it and when insulation must come off, not only on the definitions.

Injection points and mix points

API 570 treats injection points as circuits of their own because the zone where an injected stream meets the process often corrodes far faster than the line around it. Refinery examples include wash water added upstream of hydroprocessing effluent coolers to dissolve ammonium salts, and neutralisers or corrosion inhibitors added to crude unit overheads. The code recommends upstream and downstream limits for the circuit, more CMLs near the injection point and at downstream changes of direction, and a more extensive examination of the zone around the injection nozzle at scheduled inspections. Learn those limits as definitions; the exam asks them closed-book. Hot-and-cold mix points and dead legs follow the same logic: the CML goes where flow, temperature and chemistry change, not at evenly spaced intervals.

Worked example: a bare buried transfer line under Ecology's rule

A terminal's bare buried transfer line has two condition monitoring locations. The required thickness, the greater of pressure design and the owner's structural minimum, is given as 0.180 in.

  • CML A, dry ground. 0.318 in. nine years ago, 0.282 in. today. Rate = 0.036 ÷ 9 = 0.004 in. per year. Remaining life = (0.282 − 0.180) ÷ 0.004 = 25.5 years; half is 12.75 years.
  • CML B, a wet low point. 0.301 in. nine years ago, 0.229 in. today. Rate = 0.072 ÷ 9 = 0.008 in. per year. Remaining life = (0.229 − 0.180) ÷ 0.008 = about 6.1 years; half is about 3.1 years.

Under WAC 173-180-340 the line's next thickness and corrosion-rate determination is due at the more frequent of half the remaining life and five years. CML A alone would give five years, because the state ceiling beats 12.75 years; CML B governs the line at about three years. If the owner digs to repair CML B, the uncovered pipe needs an NDE check for external corrosion under the same rule. On the exam, the parallel is API 570's thickness interval, the lesser of half the remaining life and the class maximum: read every CML, take the worst, and do not average a wet low point into a dry run.

Routes into API 570 from Seattle-area trades

Eligibility combines education with experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency: one year with an engineering or technology bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education, every route but the first counting design, construction, repair, operation or inspection and including at least a year of inspection. The API 570 certification requirements page has the detail.

  • Pipefitters and welders bring repair and construction experience; many add a CWI on the way, and AWS CWI exam prep in Seattle covers that route.
  • NDT technicians who take CML readings and profile scans already know the circuits; the step up is evaluating the data and setting intervals. NDT training in Seattle covers the earlier certifications.
  • Operators from the north Sound refineries know the process, which is half of placing a CML well.
  • Terminal staff who inspect transfer lines under an API 570 programme gain qualifying experience; time spent on Part 195 mainline work may not count, and API decides.

Fitting API 570 study around Sound refinery shifts

Self-paced study suits rotating shifts. Work closed-book topics, such as piping classes, interval rules, CUI and injection-point definitions, in short sessions on days off, and keep B31.3 for longer blocks, because the open-book half rewards fast navigation of a large PDF. When a pressure design or MAWP problem will not come out, send it to the instructor with your working; the answer comes back tied to the clause. Prometric lists test centres in and around Seattle, and each API window has its own application deadline.

Sponsoring API 570 candidates around the Sound

Refinery inspection groups, terminal operators with transfer lines under Ecology's rule and contractors who work north Sound turnarounds can enrol several candidates at once. Fees are quoted on request, and each candidate applies to API on their own record. Owners who want NDE and data review on Washington piping rather than training can see API 570 piping inspection support in Washington.

faq.q: Does Ecology require API 570 inspections at Washington marine terminals?
faq.a: For transfer pipelines at Class 1 facilities, yes. WAC 173-180-340 requires those lines to be inspected in accordance with API 570, citing the 2016 edition with its addenda, and offers the rule's coating requirements for buried lines built after May 1994 as an alternative. Class 1 facilities are oil-handling sites on or near navigable waters that move oil in bulk to or from tank vessels or pipelines, which takes in the refineries and marine terminals on the Sound. Other piping on site follows the owner's own programme.

faq.q: Is the Olympic Pipeline mainline API 570 piping?
faq.a: No. The Olympic system is a hazardous liquid pipeline regulated under 49 CFR Part 195, and the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission's pipeline safety staff inspect it. API 570 covers process piping at refineries, chemical plants and terminals, so the boundary usually sits at the station or terminal valve where the facility's piping meets the pipeline. Know which side of that valve a line is on before you assign it a circuit or an interval.

faq.q: My terminal works to the API 570 edition named in Ecology's rule. Which edition do I study?
faq.a: Study the edition listed on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for the exam window you book, because that is what the questions are written from. Ecology's rule incorporates a fixed edition and changes only when the rule is amended, so your site procedure may lag the exam. Note the differences you find between the two as you study; they make good questions to send the instructor.

faq.q: Which operating temperatures does API 570 treat as susceptible to CUI?
faq.a: API 570 defines the temperature ranges where carbon steel, low-alloy steel and austenitic stainless piping are most susceptible, and sets recommended inspection extents for insulated systems in those ranges. Learn both from the edition on your effectivity sheet rather than from a summary, because the figures are examinable and editions differ. In Puget Sound service, start with traced heavy oil and asphalt lines, lines that cycle in and out of the range and damaged jacketing at supports.

faq.q: Can pipeline maintenance work count toward API 570 experience?
faq.a: It depends on what the work was. API asks for experience in the activities API 570 describes, gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Inspecting terminal transfer lines or refinery circuits under an API 570 programme fits that description; patrolling a Part 195 mainline or running its cathodic protection surveys may not, because that work follows a different regulation. Describe your duties precisely and let API decide.

faq.q: Will I need ASME B31.4 for the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Check the effectivity sheet for your window. The API 570 Body of Knowledge centres on API 570 and ASME B31.3, supported by recommended practices such as RP 571, RP 574 and RP 578 and by ASME Sections V and IX. Ecology allows transfer pipelines to be designed to B31.3 or B31.4, so you may meet B31.4 on a terminal drawing, but the examination is built on the listed documents.

faq.q: Can I keep studying for API 570 during a north Sound turnaround?
faq.a: Yes, though most candidates slow down rather than stop. Because the course is self-paced, nothing is missed while you work twelve-hour days at Anacortes or Ferndale; pick it up again after the outage. Use the turnaround itself, though: note the CMLs, injection points and dead legs you see opened, and compare what you find with how API 570 says those circuits should be inspected.
